chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who said to his wife, “O adulteress.” He said: “He is to be flogged as a hadd punishment, and separation is to be made between them after he is flogged, and she is no longer his wife.”
He said: “But if it was words that slipped from him, without his knowing anything, and he only meant to anger her by it, then separation is not to be made between them.”

key_terms.أَفْلَتَ مِنْهُ: it slipped from him unintentionally in speech
key_terms.حَدًّا: a fixed legal punishment under sacred law
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to be flogged as a prescribed punishment
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: the spouses are separated from one another

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband says to his wife, "O adulteress"?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a husband who accuses his wife of zina. It states that if he explicitly makes such an accusation, he is punished and separation follows, while if the statement was merely a baseless utterance said in anger without knowledge, separation does not occur.
